security.notes: Every Phase 3a handler in src/main/ipc/process.ts and src/main/ipc/launcher.ts calls assertRendererFrame(event) before any service work, then .parse() input via Zod, then .parse() output before return. The handler-entry .parse() is exhaustively tested at the unit layer (every reject row asserts the service was NOT called, e.g. `expect(processService.kill).not.toHaveBeenCalled()`). The launcher service's openExternal calls all funnel through `openExternalAllowlisted` from @main/security/allowlist (no direct shell.openExternal). The kill state machine uses `process.kill` (globalThis) with a Zod-validated positive-integer PID — NEVER a shell-evaluated string. Every subprocess call in ProcessService and LauncherService uses `execFile` / `spawn` with literal argv arrays — never a single shell string. The one osascript bridge in launcher.ts uses defensively quoted path/command tokens via `escapeForAppleScript` (\ → \\, " → \"); the helper is pinned by a unit test (escapeForAppleScript regression suite in launcher.spec.ts). Not a 5 because the production Electron build is still not automated-tested for non-allowlisted file:// URL rejection (carried over from Phase 1/2), AND the URL-scheme builders for vscode/cursor/zed/windsurf use encodeURI() which leaves `?` and `#` un-encoded — a path containing those characters could in theory bleed into the URL's query string or fragment when handed to shell.openExternal. The JetBrains and Sublime builders correctly use encodeURIComponent. Treated as LOW severity because (a) all paths arriving here come from the catalog DB (filesystem_scan source) — `?`/`#` in macOS paths is extremely rare, (b) shell.openExternal goes through the allowlist gate which restricts to known editor schemes, but the unit test pins the current behaviour so a future fix can't regress silently.

electron.blocker_reason: Node 21.2.0 host cannot resolve node:util#styleText required by @electron/rebuild 4.0.4 CLI; global setup at tests/e2e/_global-setup.ts unconditionally invokes pnpm electron:rebuild which fails. Workaround validated: `pnpm exec electron-builder install-app-deps` successfully rebuilds better-sqlite3 + find-git-repositories against Electron 36.9.5 ABI (NODE_MODULE_VERSION 135), and `pnpm electron:build` produces a clean out/main/index.js — so the test code itself is shippable, only the orchestration glue is blocked.

issues.description: Playwright Electron global setup (tests/e2e/_global-setup.ts) unconditionally calls `pnpm electron:rebuild`, which invokes `pnpm exec electron-rebuild -f -w better-sqlite3 -w find-git-repositories`. On Node 21.2.0 (the developer's current host) this fails with `SyntaxError: The requested module 'node:util' does not provide an export named 'styleText'` — `styleText` lands in Node 22.x. The project's engines field already says `>=20.19.0 <21 || >=22` so the dev environment is technically out of spec, but the rebuild script has a documented fallback (`electron-builder install-app-deps`) that works fine on Node 21 (manually verified during Phase 3a QE). Fix: either (a) extend scripts/rebuild-natives.mjs to try `electron-rebuild` and fall through to `electron-builder install-app-deps` on a SyntaxError/ESM-import-resolve failure, or (b) pin CI + dev docs to Node 22+. Blocks the Phase 3a E2E specs (tests/e2e/process-flow.spec.ts + tests/e2e/launcher-flow.spec.ts) from running in this environment. Reproduction: `pnpm exec playwright test --config playwright.electron.config.ts` from the project root on a Node 21.x host.

src/main/services/launcher.ts `buildEditorUrl` uses `encodeURI()` for the file:// scheme variants (vscode, cursor, zed, windsurf) — encodeURI does NOT escape `?` or `#` because they are reserved-but-allowed in a URI. A repo whose absolute path contains either character could in theory leak the rest of the path into the URL's query or fragment when shell.openExternal opens the resulting URL in the editor. macOS paths almost never contain `?` or `#` so this is LOW severity. The JetBrains and Sublime builders use `encodeURIComponent()` and correctly escape both characters — pinned by unit tests in tests/unit/main/services/launcher.spec.ts. Current behaviour is pinned so a future fix can't regress silently.

tests/e2e/process-flow.spec.ts second test ('spawned http server surfaces in /processes table') accepts the empty state as a pass when the main-side lsof poller doesn't surface the spawned child within 15 seconds. Reasoning: macOS lsof can be flaky inside sandboxed CI / when System Integrity Protection has blocked the runner from inspecting other processes' file descriptors. The parser semantics (parseLsofListen / parseLsofCwd) and the kill state machine are exhaustively pinned by tests/unit/main/services/process.spec.ts (34 unit tests, real-subprocess SIGINT happy path + SIGTERM escalation + ESRCH/EACCES branches). The E2E spec is best-effort detection coverage; if a future test environment can reliably surface a Node-spawned http listener via lsof, the warn-and-skip branch should be removed.

tests/e2e/launcher-flow.spec.ts deliberately stops short of clicking any launcher icon. Clicking 'Open in editor' / 'Open in terminal' / 'Reveal in Finder' / 'Open remote' on the test machine would spawn a real editor/terminal/Finder window or open a real GitHub URL in the user's default browser — unacceptable noise for an automated suite. The handlers themselves are pinned by tests/unit/main/ipc/launcher.spec.ts (23 tests with mocked service) + tests/unit/main/services/launcher.spec.ts (41 tests pinning the URL builders + remote-URL normalizer + AppleScript quoting). Copy-path COULD be clicked safely (it writes to the clipboard) but Playwright Electron doesn't expose clipboard reads without extra fixture work; left for a future hardening pass.
